solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Building with very loud cracking? It must be rot

indicators.note: the loud letters break open the building, sitting inside it

parts.note: a pile is a large imposing building
FF is fortissimo, the musical mark for very loud

explanation.surface: A building creaks and cracks loudly, and the onlooker concludes the timber must be rotten.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rot' is not decay here but nonsense; 'It must be' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Rot in the sense of nonsense or drivel, a colloquial synonym.

clue.text: Father taking on lively form of Fatherhood?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
pacy means fast-moving or lively

explanation.surface: A dad takes on a livelier style of parenting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fatherhood' points to the Holy Father; 'taking on' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: The office of the Pope, the Holy Father, is a form of fatherhood in a playful sense.

clue.text: Pay for some time in film

parts.note: to foot a bill is to pay for it
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Paying to appear in a film for a while.
explanation.definitionFit: Recorded film material, a length of shot movie.

clue.text: City is first item of news on the radio

indicators.note: radio is heard, so the words are spoken rather than written

parts.note: the top story leads the bulletin

explanation.surface: A city is the lead story on a radio news broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A large city in West Yorkshire in northern England.

clue.text: Heat recalling result after an international

indicators.note: after says the reversed result follows the opening pieces
recalling as calling back, so the word sum is read backwards

parts.note: a sum is the result of adding up

explanation.surface: A sports report: a heat or qualifying race whose result is remembered after an international match.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heat' looks like a race but is the definition, meaning passionate hostility.
explanation.definitionFit: Heat as hot feeling or hostility, a synonym for ill will or animosity.

clue.text: Near alcoholic drink when around special club

parts.note: nigh means near

indicators.note: around as surrounding, so the drink wraps the special letters

parts.note: a tot is a small measure of spirits

explanation.surface: A special club where you're near a drink.
explanation.definitionFit: A nightclub or venue for late entertainment, a type of club.

clue.text: Cross Frenchman working with Greek upset the French

parts.note: M is short for Monsieur
on means working or functioning

indicators.note: in a down clue upset means turned upside down, so read backwards

parts.note: le is French for the

explanation.surface: An angry Frenchman working with a Greek upsets the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' looks like angry but means a crossbreed; 'with' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog of mixed breed, a cross between different types.

clue.text: Suspicious about new drink

indicators.note: about as around, so the suspicious word goes round the letter

parts.note: shady means suspicious or dodgy

explanation.surface: Someone is wary of a new drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Beer mixed with lemonade, a type of drink.

clue.text: Admit frock's no good

indicators.note: no means the good letter is lacking from the dress

parts.note: a frock is a dress or gown; the 's is read as 'has'

explanation.surface: Someone concedes their dress is unflattering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'frock's no good' reads as frock has no G: GOWN without G.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit something is to acknowledge or confess it, a straight synonym.

clue.text: Shore resident distressed re yacht sector

indicators.note: distressed as disturbed or damaged, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A seaside resident upset about the yachting sector.
explanation.definitionFit: A black-and-white wading bird living on the seashore.

clue.text: One that could stop a clock (though it's not a hanging matter)

definitions.text: One that could stop a clock (though it's not a hanging matter)

parts.words: One that could stop a clock (though it's not a hanging matter)
parts.note: a face that could stop a clock is very ugly; the phrase for a plain person is literally not a framed painting hung on a wall

explanation.surface: A cryptic description of an ugly face.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone not good-looking, as is a face that could stop a clock.

clue.text: Issue for which snoop gathers zero information

indicators.note: gathers as takes in, so the snoop word holds the other letters

parts.note: to snoop is to pry
O looks like zero
gen is British slang for information

explanation.surface: A newspaper issue for which a snooping reporter collects nothing useful.
explanation.walkthrough: GEN is British informal for information or the facts.
explanation.definitionFit: Issue in the sense of offspring or descendants, a legal and formal synonym.

clue.text: Material in newspaper possibly backing comprehensive guide

parts.note: an organ is a publication speaking for a group, a newspaper being one example

indicators.note: backing as going backwards, so the guide's letters are read in reverse

parts.note: an A to Z is a complete guide, especially a London street atlas

explanation.surface: Some material printed in a newspaper backs a guide that covers everything.
explanation.walkthrough: An A-Z is the British street atlas of a city, hence a comprehensive guide.
explanation.definitionFit: A fine sheer stiff fabric, so an example of material or cloth.

clue.text: Form and style

definitions.meaning: a form is a school year group of pupils

explanation.surface: Two nouns about shape and manner.
explanation.definitionFit: A school year group, and also stylish quality or elegance.

clue.text: Fool called, wasting minutes — said nothing of value

parts.note: a twit is a fool

indicators.note: wasting as losing, so the minutes letter drops out of the word for called

parts.note: termed means called or named

explanation.surface: A fool phoned, used up minutes and said nothing worthwhile.
explanation.definitionFit: To chatter idly and trivially, saying nothing of substance, like birds chirping.

clue.text: Where birds perch or we perch

parts.note: the clue appears in the Daily Telegraph, so 'we' is the newspaper itself
a perch and a pole are both old units of length, five and a half yards

explanation.surface: A puzzle asking where birds rest, or where we rest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'we' is the setter's newspaper, the Telegraph; 'or' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Birds commonly sit along the wires and tops of roadside wire-carrying posts.

clue.text: Investigator regularly observed in the act

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter

explanation.surface: A detective sees a criminal caught in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Short for detective, someone who investigates crimes.

clue.text: Applauding like a cracked bell?

definitions.meaning: a cracked bell is formerly ringing, EX plus tolling

explanation.surface: A whimsical picture of clapping that sounds like a cracked bell.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits as EX (former) TOLLING: a cracked bell no longer rings.
explanation.definitionFit: Praising enthusiastically, and humorously a bell that has stopped ringing.

clue.text: US university upset, losing American in UK city

indicators.note: losing means the American letter drops out
in a down clue upset means turned over, so read backwards

parts.note: Yale is a famous American university

explanation.surface: An upset at a US university, an American lost in a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: ELAY, the reversal from 'upset', loses an A. 'in' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: A small cathedral city in Cambridgeshire, England.

clue.text: Policeman used to probe person engaged to work by Yard is making inconsistent points

indicators.note: a probe goes inside, so the policeman letters are placed within the worker

parts.note: a contractor is someone engaged to carry out work
DI is a Detective Inspector

explanation.surface: A detective investigates a workman hired by Scotland Yard, who keeps changing his story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yard' suggests Scotland Yard but is just Y; 'by' and 'is' are link.
explanation.definitionFit: Statements that contradict one another are inconsistent; the adjective describes such points.

clue.text: Sailor, one in boggy ground, shows process of absorption

parts.note: OS is an ordinary seaman

indicators.note: in places the one letter inside the bog

parts.note: a moss is a peat bog
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A sailor in a bog demonstrates soaking up water.
explanation.walkthrough: MOSS for bog is a northern British usage. 'shows' is link.
explanation.definitionFit: Gradual absorption of liquid through a membrane, or of knowledge.

clue.text: Take another approach to the manoeuvres in winter sports venue

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the venue

parts.note: an ice rink is a venue for skating

indicators.note: manoeuvres as moves about, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Changing tactics on the ice rink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'manoeuvres' looks like part of a sporting picture but is the anagram signal for the little word beside it; 'in' places the result inside the skating venue.
explanation.definitionFit: To reconsider is to think about something again with a new approach.

clue.text: Ran off, leaving person frightened

indicators.note: leaving means the person letters exit the word

parts.note: scarpered is British slang for ran away
per as in per person, each

explanation.surface: Someone ran away, abandoning a frightened companion.
explanation.walkthrough: SCARPER is British slang for flee.
explanation.definitionFit: Afraid or alarmed, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Awkward group of criminals likely to lose heart

parts.note: a gang is a band of criminals

indicators.note: losing heart means the middle letters go

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A clumsy crew of crooks who are likely to lose their nerve.
explanation.definitionFit: Tall, thin and clumsy-looking, ungainly in movement.

clue.text: Conniving policeman actually within the law, receiving money

indicators.note: receiving as taking in, so the money letter goes inside

parts.note: cop is slang for a policeman
licit means lawful, genuinely legal

explanation.surface: A crooked officer who keeps technically to the law while taking bribes.
explanation.definitionFit: Being involved with others in wrongdoing, secretly cooperating or conniving.

clue.text: Was curtailed following substantial legal opinion

indicators.note: following says the shortened word comes after the other piece

parts.note: fat as in a substantial or large amount

indicators.note: curtailed as cut short, so the word loses its last letter

explanation.surface: A weighty legal opinion was cut short.
explanation.definitionFit: A ruling on a point of Islamic law given by a recognised authority.

clue.text: Unavoidable fine should get reduced in any circumstances

parts.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, on pencils

indicators.note: reduced means cut short, losing the final letter

parts.note: at all means in any way whatever

explanation.surface: A fine that should be cut regardless, being unavoidable.
explanation.definitionFit: Fated or inevitable, an older sense of destined to happen.

clue.text: Proffer no Government support at first, appearing uneasy

indicators.note: at first says the support piece comes at the front

parts.note: a rest is a support or prop

indicators.note: no as without, so the government letter is removed

parts.note: to proffer is to give or offer

explanation.surface: Offering no support to the Government initially leaves someone looking uneasy.
explanation.definitionFit: Restless and fidgety, unable to keep still, a synonym of uneasy.

clue.text: Out to capture hearts, getting grand love

indicators.note: to capture as to hold, so the hearts letter sits inside

parts.note: out means not in
H is the abbreviation for hearts in card games
G is the abbreviation for grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A romantic sets out to win hearts and finds great love.
explanation.walkthrough: Love is a zero score in tennis.
explanation.definitionFit: Love means zero in tennis, so it is a synonym of nil or zilch.

clue.text: Regretting ditching fashionable wig

indicators.note: ditching as discarding, so the fashionable letters are dropped

parts.note: ruing means regretting
in means fashionable

explanation.surface: Someone regrets throwing away a trendy wig.
explanation.definitionFit: Rug is informal slang for a toupee or hairpiece.

clue.text: Provide blueprint for rear half of wide house?

indicators.note: the rear half is the last two of the four letters in wide

parts.note: in astrology a house is a division of the heavens, like a zodiac sign; the question mark flags the loose equivalence

explanation.surface: An architect drawing up plans for the back of a broad house.
explanation.definitionFit: To design something is to draw up its plans or blueprint.

clue.text: Chance servant will forget name

definitions.note: used adjectivally, as in a chance meeting

indicators.note: forgetting as leaving out, so the name letter is lost

parts.note: a flunkey is a liveried servant

explanation.surface: There's a chance the servant will forget someone's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Lucky or fortuitous, happening by accident, as in a chance discovery.
